subject: Transient headroom ops and autoscale granularity — draft proposal
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Zhou <amelia.zhou@velocigen.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transient headroom ops and autoscale granularity — draft proposal

Hi Amelia,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Attached is a short draft that ties the Dedicated sizing we discussed to a transient "headroom" policy and the autoscale granularity we propose for your production pools. High-level items:

- Dedicated baseline: 32 x A100 equivalents (reserved) for core ingestion pipelines.
- Transient headroom: additional 16 GPUs available as ephemeral prewarm for traffic spikes (30m retention by default).
- Autoscale granularity: 2-GPU step increments with a 90s stabilization window to avoid thrash during short spikes.
- Credit model: ephemeral usage consumes a burst credit bucket (monthly allotment) with soft overage at a discounted rate.

Attached: Redwood_Dedicated_Sizing_Matrix_VG_v1.xlsx (breakdown by workload), SLA_Addendum_Transient_Headroom_v2.pdf (draft contract language for burst credits and preemption behavior).

Can you confirm if Velocigen's runtime can tolerate a 30s cold-start for prewarmed shards beyond the initial 16 GPUs? If you want tighter tail latency during spikes we can bump the headroom or shorten the stabilization window (tradeoff is cost and higher transient capacity consumption).

Proposed next step: if procurement is happy with the draft SLA addendum, we can lock the burst credit bucket in the MSA and schedule a technical runbook handoff with Ops (30–45 minute session).

Thanks,
Marissa

Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@velocigen.com>, Velocigen Procurement <procurement@velocigen.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jul 2029 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transient headroom ops and autoscale granularity — draft proposal

Marissa,

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the matrix — looks thorough. A few notes from our side after an internal sync:

- 30s cold-start beyond prewarm is acceptable for the short-lived conversational endpoints, but our batch inference (longer runs) needs guaranteed baseline capacity.
- Can we set a rule that preemptible ephemeral GPUs never evict jobs tagged with "batch-critical"? We'll supply a tag map.
- Procurement will want clearer credit consumption telemetry (per-route breakdown) before signing the addendum. Raj is looped for procurement questions.

If you can update the SLA_Addendum with a paragraph on tagging/preemption behavior and point us to the telemetry sample (per-route token counts vs credits consumed), we can move to signature.

Thanks,
Amelia

Subject: Re: Transient headroom ops and autoscale granularity — draft proposal

Thanks Amelia — good constraints, makes sense. Quick responses inline and an updated ask: 

- Baseline for batch-critical: we'll mark the 32-GPU reserved slab as "batch-critical" so jobs with that tag are never considered for ephemeral eviction. That preserves your batch SLAs.
- Tagging/preemption: we'll add a "protected_tag" clause to the SLA addendum that specifies how protected tags are honored by the eviction algorithm. Will include the sample tag map you mentioned.
- Credit telemetry: we'll attach a sample telemetry export that shows per-route token counts and credit burn; this will be available in console as a CSV (and pushed to your S3 if preferred).

Action items for Velocigen: please share the initial tag map and confirm the monthly burst-credit budget range you're comfortable committing to (we suggested 1.5x baseline token throughput in the spreadsheet).

Internal note for Ops/legal: Ben/Karthik — Ben please review the "protected_tag" contract language and confirm that our eviction logic accepts a simple allowlist of tags (we can document behavior: eviction ignores jobs with protected tags except during extreme capacity events defined as >95% sustained utilization for 60m). Karthik, can you flag any pricing implications for granting S3 telemetry exports and per-route breakdowns? Lauren — can you prepare a short technical runbook template for the handoff session (30–45m) that covers tagging, preemption, and how to interpret the CSV telemetry?

I'll await the tag map from Velocigen and then circulate a revised SLA_Addendum.

Best,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2029 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Transient headroom ops and autoscale granularity — draft proposal (internal)

Marissa / team — quick internal follow-up after reading Amelia's ask:

- Eviction behavior: confirming we support a protected_tag allowlist. Implementation note: protected_tag evaluation happens at allocation time; if a protected job is already running it remains until completion unless we hit an extreme overload condition (>95% sustained for 60m) where we escalate to manual ops.
- Telemetry export: per-route token/credit CSV is cheap to produce and we can include a sample in the revised doc. No additional recurring charge, but large S3 transfer will be billed per the existing infra terms (flag to pricing).
- Pricing implication: Karthik — if we provide 1.5x burst-credit headroom and include S3 telemetry exports, recommend we price the burst-credit tier conservatively (suggest baseline price + 20% uplift for the added telemetry/ops SLA).

I'll draft suggested contract language for the protected_tag paragraph and attach to the revised SLA_Addendum.

Ben
